previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and dehydration in the setting of multiple myeloma and immunocompromise. He had not taken his Revlimid recently and presented with symptoms suggestive of a gastrointestinal infection, possibly viral or bacterial, with reactive joint pain. Workup included negative CT head and chest X-ray, and CT abdomen showed persistent but improved colonic thickening, likely from resolving diverticulitis or colitis. Stool studies were negative for pathogens. He was treated with IV fluids, Ciprofloxacin, and Metronidazole for presumed gastroenteritis. His supratherapeutic INR of 3.3 led to a temporary hold on warfarin, with resumption at 5 mg nightly; ultrasound confirmed a non-occlusive DVT in the right femoral and popliteal veins. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, adjusted warfarin, and home medications with instructions to follow up with his PCP and oncologist.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Chest frontal and lateral views.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Frequent falls.

___.

FINDINGS:  The cardiac silhouette is mild to moderately enlarged.  Mediastinal
contours are stable.  No focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or evidence of
pneumothorax is seen.  There is no overt pulmonary edema.  No definite
displaced fracture is identified.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

EXAM:  Non-contrast-enhanced CT of the head.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Multiple falls, question head strike, evaluate for
intracranial hemorrhage.

___.  

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast-enhanced MDCT images of the head were obtained. 
Reformatted coronal and sagittal images were also obtained.  

TOTAL EXAM DLP:  1003.42 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, midline
shift, mass effect, or acute large vascular territorial infarct.  Old left
putamen infarct is again seen.  Minimal periventricular white matter
hypodensities likely reflect sequela of small vessel disease.  There is no
hydrocephalus.  Very minimal mucosal thickening is seen in the left maxillary
sinus.  The remainder of the visualized paranasal sinuses are clear.  The left
mastoid is underpneumatized.  Again, the left middle ear cavity is partially
opacified, similar to prior suggesting chronic infection/inflammatory process.
The right mastoid air cells are clear.  No acute fracture is seen.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process. 
 
Again seen underpneumatized left mastoid air cells with opacity seen in the
left middle ear cavity, similar to prior, suggesting chronic
inflammatory/infectious process.

EXAMINATION:  MR thoracic and lumbar spines

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with IgA MM with relapse with recurrent falls and
left foot numbness with hx of T12 "blast fracture" s/p radiation therapy in
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar, multi sequence MR images of the thoracic and lumbar
spine were obtained before and after the administration of intravenous
contrast.

COMPARISON:  CT chest ___ and ___. CT abdomen/pelvis ___.

FINDINGS: 

Thoracic spine: Within the anterior superior T12 vertebral body, there is a 15
mm region which demonstrates low signal intensity on T1 and T2 weighted
images.  There is surrounding associated STIR hyperintensity, and mild loss of
height of the vertebral body. The appearance is unchanged from the previous
chest CTs. No other lesion is identified. There is otherwise diffuse fatty
replacement of the bone marrow.

Thoracic spine alignment is maintained. Scattered thoracic spine degenerative
changes are present most significant at T11-T12 where there is a small disc
protrusion, but there is no significant spinal canal or neural foraminal
narrowing.

The thoracic cord is normal in morphology and signal intensity. There is no
evidence for cord compression.

Lumbar spine: Lumbar spine alignment is maintained. Vertebral body heights and
disc spaces are preserved. There is diffuse increased signal of the bone
marrow compatible with fatty replacement. No abnormal enhancement or
suspicious bone lesion is identified.

The conus medullaris is normal in morphology and signal intensity and
terminates at the level of L1.

T12-L1 and through L2-L3: There are facet degenerative changes without
significant spinal canal or neural foraminal narrowing.

L3-L4: There is a mild diffuse disc bulge, facet hypertrophy and thickening of
the ligamentum flavum causing mild narrowing of the subarticular recesses.
There is moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing, right greater than
left.

L4-L5: There is a diffuse disc bulge, facet hypertrophy and thickening of the
ligamentum flavum causing mild spinal canal narrowing. The disc bulge contacts
the traversing L5 nerve roots. The small bilateral facet joints effusions are
present, and there is a small, oblong synovial cyst extending from the right
facet joint. Moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing is present, left
slightly greater than right.

L5-S1: There is a diffuse disc bulge which extends into the right neural
foramen greater than left and facet degenerative changes. The spinal canal is
patent. There is mild left and severe right neural foraminal narrowing with
likely compression of the exiting right L5 nerve root.

IMPRESSION:


1. T12 vertebral body compression with mild loss of height of the T12
vertebral body, unchanged from the prior chest CTs. No other lesion is
identified. There is no evidence for cord compression.
2. Multilevel lumbar spine degenerative changes with severe right neural
foraminal narrowing at L5-S1 levels as described above.
